Introduction This repair manual microfiche is to assist you in performing the necessary maintenance and repair work expertiy and correctly. It must be placed at the disposal of shop foremen and mechanics, and will complement the practical and theoretical training offered by our Service Training Centre. Since 1985 models there are two repair manuals. * — Repair manual to models * Repair manual to construction groups The Construction Group Repair Manual consists of Groups 11, 12, 13, 23, 24 and 33, It is independent of models and describes repairing procedures on removed components and provides testing instructions and troubleshooting tables. A Model Repair Manual ('3' Series, ‘5S’ Series, ‘6’ Series or ‘7’ Series) contains all construction groups. The descriptions in the above mentioned construction groups refer chiefly to removing and installing of replacing procedures. There are technical data and nominal value microfiches for specifications and adjusting values. Application of this repair manual microfiche is in reference to a standard production car free from accident damage and not subsequently modified In any way. The construction group system has been adopted from the flat rate manual. The job numbers used in the text are meant for use as cross reference. They will frequently contain job procedures, which must not be used for extension of the flat rates. They are only provided to make finding of repair procedures easier. The individual page numbering, for example 32 — 6, means: 32 + main group 6 - page number The special tools essential for correct repair work are summarized on the special tool microfiche, Order No. 01 99 9 699 422. Their use is illustrated in the descriptions of the various repair jobs. The removal work is described for each repair job in this manual. If installation does not take place in the reverse order of work, an “Installation” note is provided. In addition to the improvements supplied to you regularly in the form of “Service Information”, you are racommended to consult the parts microfiches for additional illustrated data. 1165020 REMOVING AND INSTALLING TURBOCHARGER The turbocharger receives oil from the engine oil circuit. The following points are important to guarantee sufficientlubrication for the fast running turbocharger. — Engine oil circuit in pertect condition (specified engine oil, oi! level, crankcase venting, etc.). ~ Engine not raced before building up engine oil pressure (control lamp) — engine also not stopped at high speed (turbocharger keeps on running). ~ Engine not started immediately after an oi! change, but instead oil pressure built up first by cranking engine with the starter (fuel shutoff electric lead disconnected — see 11 00 039). s: Working instructions for engune electrical and ignition systems
t: WORKING INSTRUCTIONS FOR ENGUNE ELECTRICAL AND IGNITION SYSTEMS (TCI = Transistor Coil Ignition and DME = Digital Motor Electronics) Always disconnect the battery or interrupt power supply to the control unit and ignition coil when working on the electrical system, charging the battery or welding on the car — danger from primary and secondary voltage in engine and general electrical equipment (e.g. alternator) Never start the engine after removing the distributor cap or disconnecting the wire on ignition coil terminal 4 — pull off plug on ignition control unit. Never disconnect the battery or wires on the alternator and starter while the engine is runrung. ~ Only use specified original BMW parts. Never connect a shielded capacitor or test lamp on terminal 1 of the ignition coil, Never connect terminal 1 of the ignition coil with ground or B +. Consequently when service installing a burglar alarm system, the terminal 1 wire must not be used for startér interlocking. ~ Pull off the control unit plug in cars with TCI or the fuel injection master relay (relay 2) in cars with DME when checking the compression. The secondary (high voltage) side of the ignition system must be shielded with at least 4 k-ohms, whereby the original distributor rotor with 1 k-ohm must be installed. Never use a 5 k-ohm distributor rotor for interference suppression of a radio or communication set!

Dangerous high tension voltage in engine and car electrical systems (e.g. on the tachometer), — The secondary (high tension) side of the ignition system must have a load of at least 4 k-ohms. — The engine must not be started as long as the distributor cap is removed or the electric lead is disconnected on ignition coil terminal 4. — Neither shielded capacitors nor test lamps may be connected on terminal 1 of the ignition coil, — Electric lead of ignition coil terminal 1 must never be connected on ground or 8B + Therefore the terminal 1 lead may not be used to interlock engine starting when service installing a burglar alarm system. — Never disconnect the battery or electric leads on the alternator and starter while the engine is running.

t: 12-111/8 IDLE SPEED CONTROL, SPEED LIMIT, COLD START CONTROL Reter to E 34 diagnosis test plan in chapter 1210 OME M 13, TYPES OF INJECTION Each group of fuel Injectors (2+ 4 or 1 + 3) Is activated by a final stage (current amplifier). It ts theretore possible to divide the injection cycle Into groups of cylinders. This guarantees limited engine operation even when one group falls. Semi-sequential injection: There Is injection In one group of cylinders (2 + 4 or 1 + 3) only once every 720 crankshall degrees as from an engine speed of 600 rpm. This timing can func- tion only when the DME control unit receives a signal fram the camshall send- er (on camshaft sprocket of exhaust valves). Timing remains In semi-sequential Injection if the signal Is received later. Parallel Injection: Parallel injection means simultaneous activation of all fuel injectors for each Crankshaft revolution and takes place only when the camshaft sender has not put out any signats since starting the engine. if a signal Is put out later, the system switches over lo semi-sequential injec- tlon a& $00n as an engine speed of 2500 rpm Is exceeded. IGNITION Stationary ignition Distribution: Each cylinder has its own ignition coll. in this manner the sysiem of rotating ignition distribution Is omitted. DME activates each ignition coll separately. Double ignition: Double ignition means activation of the spark plugs for éach crankshall revo- lution and takes place only when the camshaft sender does not put oul signals. Switching over from normal to double ignition, or vice versa, takes place im- mediately in contradiction to fuel injection. ANTL-KNOCK FUNCTION The ignition timing is retarded depending on intake alt and engine temperature, in order to prevent seif-ignition of the tuelair mixture In the combustion chamber (knocking). CATALYTIC CONVERTER PROTECTION There is danger of overheating the catalytic converter when the catalytic con- werter protection Is active over a long period of time. For this reason the fuel | alr mixture is enriched to reduce (he exhaust gas temperature. THROTTLE VALVE POTENTIOMETER A throttie valve potentiometer !s instalied instead of a throttle valve switch with Idle and tull load contacts, This potentiometer must mo longer be adjusted, since DME learns the Idle speed Ignition timing (idle speed switching point) on its own. DME adds a determined value to the learned value. This value must go owe potentiometer to OME In order to be processed as a full load signal in DM AIR CONDITIONER COMPRESSOR SHUTOFF In order to have the entire engine power for drive while moving olf, the air conditioner compressor is switched off for up to 7 seconds at road speeds of <8 kevh (5 mph) and simultaneous full load state. t: 12-112/4 TROUBLESHOOTING DME 1.7 M 42 Note Always conform with safety and accident prevention regulations for all tests and work on the engine electric and electronic system. Caution! Dangerous high tension on primary and secondary circuits of ignition. The battery should not be disconnected whenever possible, since otherwise this would cancel the faults stored In memorles of all control units. Disconnect contro! units on wire harness only with the ignition turned off. Test electric leads only with disconnected control unit or component plugs. Testing Means: Wiring diagrams can be found in “General Car Electrical System - 3 Series” files. Only use qualilied testing leads, terminals and clips. Use 88-pin test adapter set 61 4 410. Multimeter Presentation of a memory-stored fault on screen. Location of Fault: ‘The number of a fault refers to the pin connection on the contro! unit. A fault could be on a.component, concerned electric leads or in the control unit. Type of Fault: Shorts, breaks, exceeding of ranges or implausible functions are displayed. Frequency: Information whether or not (brief fault) a fault exists at the moment of time. Also display of how often the fault was recognized. If the fault no longer exists, the number of times the engine had been started since the last recognition of the fault is displayed. Recognition During: Additional fault information about the operating conditions during recognition of a fault. List of Faults: Faults stored in memories can be displayed on the tester by selecting 900 (Fault Memory). No faults stored In memories. Function disturbed: engine operation not possible. t: 17— 3.1 Cooling Circull - M49 1 Cap with pressure relief and vacuum valves: From engine Bleeding hose Control hose To water pump 2 3 4 To Thermostat 5 6 7 Level marks The bypass principle Is applied in order to have good alr exclusion in the cooling circuit. Use of a cross-flow radiator permits integration of the bypass expansion tank on the side of the radiator. The tank Is designed two-plece In order to have sufficient tank volume. This version permits use of transparent plastic in the area of level marks. The bleeding hose mouths below the minimum level mark. In this manner air excluded from the bypass tank Is prevented from tlowing back into the full flow circuit when unscrewing the tank cap. The pressure relief valve in the tank cap Is activated via a control hose by radiator feed pressure. The cooling system Is protected against excessive operating pressure registering the radiator feed pressure. Pimasns jOCNE tin paoes er approximately the amount of the radiator operating pressure during the after-heating phase. This Improves the operating safety of the cooling system and the bolling-over safety while after-heating.

If only one axle turns in a test on the brake test stand, the central lock will be subjected to strong loads and could be destroyed from excessive heat. t: 30 31534 31-42 3. Backlash Adjustment for Ring Gear/Pinion Mount dial gage 00 2 510 and Special Too! 00 2 500, with dial gage point at right angle to tooth, and measure play. Nominal value". Backlash excessive = instal! thicker shim (C). Backlash insufficient = install thinner shim (C). Change shims until nominal value is reached. Note: The difference between the actyal backlash and nominal backlash*, multiplied by the factor 1,15, produces the amount of which shim (C) must be thicker or thinner. Example: Measured backlash 0.19 mm (0.0075") — specified min. play 0.06 mm (0.0024) Difference 0.13 mm (0.0051") Difference x factor = 0.13 mm x 1.15 = 0.15 mm or 0.0051” x 1.15 = 0.0059”. * See Specifications The thickness of installed shim (C)_@.9 2.01 mm (0.079"'), must be increased by 0.15 mm (0.006*). Shims are available in thickness steps of 0,03 mm (0.0012"}. Important! The total thickness of shims (B + C) must not be changed. If, for example, the thickness of shim (C) 1s reduced, the thickness of shim (B) must be increased by the same amount, or vice versa. s: Adjustments on front axle final drive
t: 31-43 4, Tooth Contact Pattern Type of teeth — Gleason, (Coat ring gear with printer's ink, Turn differential several times in both directions and stop ring gear suddenly with a piece of wood. BASIC INFORMATION FOR TOOTH CONTACT PATTERN ADJUSTMENTS Gleason Teeth Correct tooth contact pattern without load. A1 Loads will displace the tooth contact pattern slightly more toward the outside. Moving the ring gear will mainly change the backlash and also the tooth contact Pattern in longitudinal direction of the teeth. Mowing the drive pinion will change the tooth contact pattern in direction of tooth height, while the backlash will be changed only slightly. Here are the four basically wrong tooth contact patterns, which normally occur in combination and the knowledge of which will make practical adjustments eaner. 1. High, narrow tooth contact pattern (head) on ring gear. Move drive pinion toward ring gear axis and possibly correct backlash by pressing ring gear away from drive pinion, 2, Deep, narrow tooth contact pattern (base) on ring gear, Move drive pinion away from ring gear axis and possibly corcect backlash by pressing ring gear closer, 3. Brief tooth contact pattern on small tooth end (tip) of ring gear, Move ring gear away from drive pinion. Wf applicable, move drive pinion closer to ring gear axis, 4. Brief tooth contact pattern on large tooth end (hee!) of ring gear. Move ring gear closer to drive pinion. Vf applicable, move drive pinion away from ring gear axis, 27833050

32-5la 4. Scrapping “Airbag” Vehicles: In accordance with accident prevention regulations “airbag” gas generators must be rendered unusable prior to scrapping. This is necessary since the gas generator is 3 Pyrotechnical object and could cause injury if activated incorrectly (for example with 8 torch during scrapping). Airbag gas generators must be ignited in the vehicles meant for scrapping from the outside and with doors of vehicles closed. The igniter, Special Too! 62 1 270, developed by BMW must be dsed for this purpose. Non-ignited generators are a source of danger (also for the environment)! 1, Remove lower section of steering column casing and disconnect airbag plug (orange). 2. Connect airbag plug and igniter together. 3. Connect igniter on a 12 V battery placed 10 meters (32 feet) away from car. 4. Keep as far away from car as the length of the igniter’s lead — always stand in front of car (this also concerns other persons). 5. Operate switch of igniter. Caution! The burning off of the solid fuel will heat the airbag unit — danger of burning hands! Wash hands after touching ignited generators!

s: Braking and cateral forces in relation to slip
t: 34-22 1. ANTIBLOCK SYSTEM (ABS) —- DESCRIPTION AND DESIGN BRAKING AND CATERAL FORCES IN RELATION TO SLIP Description: The basis of a braking action is the friction between the tires and road surfaces. To brake a vehicle the tires havé to transmit a frictional force to the road surface. In so doing there will be slip between the tires and road surface, i.e. the tire peripheral velocity will be slower than the road speed of the vehicle. Figure 730 34 112 shows the relation between the frictional force and slip for a typical case on a dry road surface. The transmitted braking force reaches its maximum value in shaded area A. This is also the control range of ABS. When a wheel is locked, i.e. when there is 100% slip, the frictional force will normally be lower than when a wheel is rolling. oH WT Consequently the ABS must control the brake pressure in the wheel brake cylinder in such a manner that the slip remains in the shaded area, because here the highest frictional force is available. yy, 7 N At the same time there will then be sufficient lateral cornering force to guarantee steering and directional stability. AX The amount of slip, with which there is maximum frictional force, and the amount of frictional force itself depend chiefly on the tires (type, treads, rubber composition), the road surface (material, surface condition, wet, ice), the road speed and the slip angle of the wheels. 100 */e - —— G mm HN The ABS detects the frictional conditions between the tires and road surface prevailing at the moment, It automatically adjusts to each change in road surface/tire relation and makes use of the highest coefficient of friction, without that the vehicle slips or skids because of wheel locking. mo uo o Non-uniform friction conditions between the separate wheels will be held under control just as also instantaneous changes in the road surfaces, e.g. through patches of ice. t: 34 - DESIGN The ABS consists of a control unit, hydraulic unit, speed sensors and a wire harness, Components are described separately below . Speed Sensors: Each speed sensor has a gear wheel, which runs past the permanently magnetized edge of the speed sensor and is installed in the wheel hubs. The rotary motion of the wheels is recorded by inductive sensors and an electric signal is sent to the electronic control unit. Electronic Control Unit: The electronic control unit is located in the passenger compartment on left side underneath instrument panel. In a small multi-channel electronic computer accelration, decelration and slip factors are derived from the electric signals of the speed sensors, which are proportional to the wheel velocity. By logical connection of these factors there are control commands for the electromagnetically operated valves in the hydraulic unit. The signal processing in the computer determines the contro! behavior of the system. The expected degree of dependavility is based on digital engineering with highly integrated circuitry. The control unit contains electronic monitoring circuits, which control the function prior to each trip and the ABS wire harness with equipment constantly during a trip. If the control unit detects @ defect in the wire harness or electrical part of the equipment, the monitoring circuit will switch off the ABS and guarantee normal use of the brake system. An ABS indicator lamp reports this condition to the driver. 23 Hydraulic Unit: The hydraulic unit 1s located in the engine compartment and was added to the conventional brake system, To control the brake pressure in the wheel brake cylinders, the brake hydraulic unit has threeway valves which permit three brake pressure conditions. Pressure build-up, pressure holding and pressure drop. These three pressure phases adapt themselves in the sequences and length to the requirements of the desired control characteristic and power flow between the road surface and tires, In principle the contro! procedures are as follows. As soon as a wheel deceleration or slip indicates the locking of a wheel, the brake pressure is first held. If the wheel still tends to lock, the pressure will be dropped so long until the. wheel accelerates or the slip limit is exceeded. Afterwards the pressure is raised again and the contro! phases begin from new. An electrically driven return delivery pump returns the brake fluid taken from the wheel brake cylinder while dropping the pressure to the appropriate brake circuit. The pump is designed as a two-piston pump so that the circuits of a dual brake circuit system remain fully separated. Wire Harness: The control unit is connected with the speed sensors and electric part of the hydraulic unit via a special wire harness for the sake of signal input and order output as well as electric power supply.

s: Description and duty of acceleration pick-up (325 1X)
t: 34-28 DESCRIPTION AND DUTY OF ACCELERATION PICK-UP (325 1X) Description: In the acceleration pick-up there are two mercury switches, one each for forward and reverse drive, which are installed in longitudinal direction of car at on angle to the horizontal. The series connected mercury switches provide closed contact in horizontal position (resistance less than 1 k-ohm). Negative acceleration (braking) of the car or inclination of the acceleration transmitter will displace the mercury filling and cause the contact to open (resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms). The glass tube is inclined in such a manner, that braking deceleration of 35 to 45 % is necessary to- open the contact. The braking deceleration value for forward drive can be simulated by inclining the acceleration pick-up from 19.5 to 24° (with Special Tool 34 5 150 this is equal to 26.5 to 33.0 mm (1.043 to 1,299"), The switching point for reverse drive does not have to be adjusted. Duty: BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive) is the first standard production car to have permanent all wheel drive with constantly switched central and rear axle locks and also a continuously effective ABS. So that all three systems can be effective simultaneously, a sensor is required to provide information on the road condition (higher or lower traction). The acceleration pick-up performs this duty in the BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive). The ABS contro! unit will decide between various data fields depending on the switch condition (open or closed mercury switches), and consequently consider the traction condition of a street or road, Defective Indicator: If an open switch condition (resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms) is reported to the ABS control unit over 3 period of time longer than 20 seconds, the ABS switches off and reports this to the driver with a warning lamp in the instrument cluster.

However, also make sure that the machine Is In perfect condition and that the wheel rim and tire are not damaged. General Tire Removing / Mounting Instructions Removing: Begin removal of a tire at the valve. After pressing the tire off of the rim flange, remove balance weights, press tire bead Into well and coat thoroughly with tire mounting paste**. Clean wheel rim thoroughly and inspect rim for damage before mounting tire. The valve and valve insert must be replaced each time a tubeless tire is re- moved and Installed. Important! Loosen the tire on the inside and outside by applying the pressing-off horn on.the bead periphery at several points before pressing off the tire. Should it be difficult to press off the tire, pry the tire away from the rim flange as far as poss-ible with the pressing-off horn and then apply tire mounting paste between the tire and rim flange. Repeat this step around the complete periphery of the tire. Then press of the tire completely. Greater pressing-off force Is required for “TD tires” due to the bead toe seal. It is necessary to loosen tire on Inside and outside at several points around the bead periphery with the pressing-off horn prior to pressing off. Caution! TD bead toe could jump out of Denloc groove suddenly and cause pressing-off horn to knock in! Mounting; Coat tire bead with tire mounting paste**. Make sure tire Is mounted on correct side, especially in case of asymmetric tires. The “outside” of these tires is marked. Mount tire with as little as possible stress on the beads, since otherwise there would be danger of damaging the tire or TD bead toe of TD tires. First of all let the tire bead ~ coming from the well — jump over the hump of the rim-shoulder. inflate the tire in steps while observing continuously. Maximum “jump-over pressure” = 3.3 bar (47 psi). Hf the tire Is not seated on the rim correctly, increasing the inflation pressure will not improve the tire seating! Instead it will be necessary to press off both tire beads, apply another coat of tire mounting paste and to Inflate Ue tire again. increase the Inflation pressure slowly until the tire “settles” only when the beads bear on the rim shoulders correctly. Maximum “settling pressure” = 4.0 bar (57 psi). Refer to Service Information of Group 36 for approved tires, tire sizes and wheel rims as well as special equipment. We must point out that TD tires may be mounted only on TD rims! Incorrect mounting of TD tires on rims of other design (even TR!) could cause'tire damage, which in turn could lead to tire blowout while driving car. Such tires may never be reused, not even on TD rims! ** Source of Supply: HWB

DESCRIPTION OF ELECTRONIC ABSORBER CONTROL (EDC) Three different shock absorber settings (comfort, normal and sport) can be selected with a switch in the middle console, The shock absorber selection is indicated with control lamps in the ihstrument cluster, An additional contro! lamp (absorber symboi) indicates faults in the electrical system. The system monitor control lamp goes out about 1.5 seconds after turning on the ignition. Fault reports can be cancelled after elimination of the cause by turning the ignition off and on. Shock absorber settings (bump and rebound stages) are controlled by solenoids on the double-pipe 92s pressure shock absorbers. The control unit monitors the same setting of all shock absorbers. In case of a fault in the electrical system there is automatic switchover to sport for safety’s sake [all solenoids are without current). There is also switchover to sport, if a speedometer signal is missing (car stopped; Vo limit, time delay approx. 1.5 sec.). The system switches back to the selected shock absorber setting as soon as there is a signal again (moving off) within approximately 0.05 seconds, There is speed-dependent regulation in the comfort position, There is automatic switchover from comfort to normal setting at a road speed of about 110 km/h (68 mph). It switches back to comfort when the road speed drops below about 100 km/h (62 mph). Automatic switchovers are not displayed by the contro! lamps, since the control lamps only show the Position of the selector switch,

37-15 RIDE LEVEL CONTROL / CIRCULATING SYSTEM Description Ride control has the task of keeping the rear end of the car at a certain level regardless of the payload (up to maximum axle load). A piston-type pump bolted on the power steering pump provides the system with necessary pressure. The flow of oil produced permanently by the pump is distributed to the line leading to the pressure reservoirs and a return line by a mechanically operated regulating valve depending on payload and ride level. Ride level information for the regulating valve is taken from the rear axle stabilizer. Loading the car causes the suspension to bottom and in turn the stabilizer to turn. A control valve in the regulating valve is turned to lift position with help of a lever with regulating rod. The turning of the stabilizer is reduced as the rear end of the car lifts, which in turn means that the control valve in the regulating valve is also turned back to normal position continuously. After reaching the nominal ride tevel the control valve will be back in normal position and the oil flows direct into return (circulation). After reaching the maximum permissible rear axle load, a pressure safety valve in the regulating valve prevents a further increase of pressure in spring struts and pressure reservoirs, so that the rear end of an overloaded car will drop. The stabilizer is turned in opposite direction when unloading the car. The control valve in the regulating valve is turned to lower position, so that the oil under pressure in spring struts and pressure reservoirs can flow into return. The control valve will be back in normal position after reaching the nominal ride level. A. low pressure valve in the regulating valve prevents dropping the pressure in spring struts and pressure reservoirs below the minimum pressure while lifting the car. The oil forced out by piston rods of single-pipe shock absorbers is pushed back and forth between the spring struts and pressure reservoirs while driving each time the suspension of rear wheels bottoms and rebounds. The gas cushion of the pressure reservoirs is then compressed and released alternately, producing the effect of gas pressure struts, which is applied parallel to the coil springs of the spring struts.

41-001 INTRODUCTION This repair manual for body jobs |s supplicd for skilled workers and consequently It Is assumed, thal persons referring to this manual will be well qualified, conscientious workers with the necessary amount of responsibility. Instructions are therefore limited to information on factory approved repair methods as well as related tips and working alds. The described body repair jobs refer to the complete or partial replacement of parts with original BMW replacement parts or sections of replacement parts. Straightening and dent removal must be adapted to a pertinent damage scope. Concerned welding and spot welding seams must be inspected and, If necessary, repaired. Reler to the cut out parts for the quantity and location of welding spots, Inert gas welded seams and brazed conneciions. Use inert gas plug welding Instead of spot welding In non-accessible areas. Most pictures show a rough, unpainted bodyshell. Remove or cover all car parts, which are in the repair zone and are In danger of belng subjected to heat, sparks or dust. Disconnect the ground lead on the battery or body connection point. Protect electric leads against dangers of mechanical or thermal influence. Conform with safety precautions for cars with an airbag system (SRS). Conform with fire and accident prevention regulations. Welding can be performed after removal of control units, If - there is guarantee of about 1 meter (3 feet) distance between welding and ground connections and - there*is guarantee of good electric connection between welding and ground points (no rubber mounts or anything similar). if not, thermal development must be considered especially In case of autogen welding (decisions must be made for each Individual case). In spite of continuous quallty control in welding by the factory, it is still possible that some welded points could be faulty. They will be repaired in the factory subsequently, elther with inert gas spot welding or, when not accessible, with 15 mm (0.590") long Inert gas welded seams on the flange end. Consequently repaired welded seams on the body do not always Indicate repairs by a third party. For example: lett engine carrier member resistance spot welded - right engine carrier member welding repaired with inert gas welding. Important! The steering gear must be inspected and maybe replaced after an accident or accident-similar driving conditions - see Service Information 32 01 88 (828). Seal off all sealing seams, sealed In original state, with a body sealing compound. Replace damaged anti-drumming insulation. Seal new sheet metal parts or the cavities, seams, creases and folds produced by new sheet metal parts with a body sealing compound Immediately. RECOMMENDED WORKING METHODS AND TOOLS 1. Cutting Out Damaged Parts: Determine the location of mating surfaces with help of the replacement part before beginning with the work. Cut out damaged part roughly within the mating surfaces. Caution! Don't damage sheet metal located underneath. Remove sealing compound, antl-drumming compound and, If applicable, paint to neutralize the connection points. Drill out spot welding. Make sure holes are drilled In the cut out part while drilling. Don't drill In the connection flanges remaining for installation of the new part. Grind off wefded seams with a dise grinder carefully. Heat brazed connections with an aulogen gas torch (don't heat excesslvely!). Lift off scrap metal. Remove residual brazing solder with a steel brush. Straighten and grind all connection points thoroughly. 2. Installing New Parts: Prepare connection points to pertinent repairing Instructions. Always perform repairs, which concem the suspension points of the engine, Creatas ah coitinnl Gane. Feeer to parkoean seaminge tor tas ghee of wake, engine hood and trunk Ild. Coat mating surtaces Intended for resistance spot welding with zinc dust paint. Only remove the protective paint from galvanized replacement parts. Drill 8 mm (0.315") dia. holes with same spacing as the drilled out welded spots In connec- tions not accessible for the spot welding tongs and Insert gas plug weld. “tats 41-0021 Produce Inert gas welded seams according to the part cut out. Produce brazed connections with as little as possible heat dispersion and without excessive heat. Procedures deviating from standard connections will be described In the repair manual. Grind down welded seams visible on outside surfaces. Caution! Don't grind down the sheet metal too thin. Straighten and tin out Irregularities. Tinning out Is supposed to prepare the surface to such an extent, that only a coat of fine filler has to be applied prior to spraying on paint. Seal off all welding seams, which had been sealed In original state, with a body sealing compound, Replace damaged anti-drumming compound. Seal new sheet metal parts or the cavities, seams, creases and folds produced by new sheet metal parts with a body cavity sealing compound immediately. If dust has gotten In eyes, rinse out thor- oughly with water and go to a physician. Dab coated skin and wash thoroughly with water and soap. If great amount of vapors are Inhaled, go outdoors In the fresh air and, if necessary, visit a physician. Information on Toxicology: Systems containing styro! will irritate eyes, skin and the respiratory track. No damaging effects are known from decades of use as long as handling Is correct. Measures In Case of Fire; Fire extingulshing agents: water mist'(no water stream), powders, foam, CO2 and halon. 54-29 ELECTRIC / HYDRAULIC CONVERTIBLE TOP Description: it is only possible to operate the top In a stopped car and with the ignition on, and Operation lasts only as long as the operating switch In the dashboard Is pressed. The switch Is Iiluminated when lights are switched on. All windows must be wound down and the trunk lid closed. If the car Is moved off with an unlocked top, the top will be run back Into the top box (not when the top lid Is already locked). An Indicator lamp in the Instrument cléuster sends Information to the driver with the ignition turned on. 1) On Continuously: During top operation ((switch pressed - top moving) 2) Continuous Flashing: Don't move off! 64 - 01 Description of Integrated Heating and Air Conditioning System The heating system is an air side controlled unit, i.e. the temperature is regulated by the mixing ratio of cold and warm air with help of the temperature mixing flap. All outletscan be heated. Flaps are operated via cables. The water flow rate through the heater #s regulated by an electromagnetic water valve in the water return circuit, It is switched on and off by the temperature control via a track circuit with loop contact, The valve will be closed when the temperature control is set to < 20° C (68° F). The valve is open without electric power, With air conditioning the refrigerant is injected via an expansion valve, which is located in the housing on the right side, A mechanical thermostat switch, located on left side of the unit, is applied for protection against freezing. With air conditioning the fresh air/circulated air can be operated for extremely fast cooling of the passenger compartment or elimination of disturbing odors. The flaps are located in front of both blowers and are operated by two positioning motors. Air conditioning equipment includes an additional two-speed electric fan. This fan always runs at least in first speed when the air conditioner is switched on. Regardless of air conditioner operation 1st speed of extra fan is switched on as from a coolant temperature of 89 ... 93° C (192 ... 199° F) and switched off with a coolant temperature of 86 ... 82° C (187 ... 180° F). Regardless of air conditioner operation 2nd speed of extra fan is switched on as from a coolant temperature of 97 ... 101° C (207 ... 214° F) and switched off with a coolant temperature of 94 ... 90° C (201 ... 194° F). The drief has one high pressure and one low pressure safety switch. The high pressure switch stops the compressor when reaching a coolant pressure of 25.5 ... 17.7 bar (363 ... 252 psi) and switches the compressor on again when coolant pressure drops to 22.5 .., 20 bar (320 ... 284 psi). The low pressure switch stops the compressor when coolant pressure drops to 2.22 ... 1.72 bar (32 ... 24 psi) and switches the compressor on again when coolant pressure rises to 2.0 ... 2.4 bar (28 ... 34 psi). These safety switches prevent damage in or on the air conditioning system. Heating and Air Conditioning Controls + Consisting of: Temperature Control The temperature control regulates the temperature regulating Hap via a cable and opens the water valve at an angle of > 20°. Air Volume Control Switch It switches the blower in 3 speeds via fixed resistors, which are located in the heater. Air Up Control Lever It operates via a cable the flap in the heater/air conditioner for air distribution to the windsmeld (defrost). Air Center Control Lever It operates via a cable the flap in the heater/air conditioner for air distribution out of the instrument panel nozzles (ventilation). With air conditioning the control lever will also have a circuit breaking switch (track circuit) for the compressor. The compressor will be switched off with a flap opening of < 20 %, to avoid liquid knocks in the air conditioner which could destroy the compressor. Air Down Control Lever It operates via a cable the flap in the heater/air conditioner for air distribution down to the footwells. With air conditioning the control lever will have the same compressor circuit breaking switch as for the air center control lever. A/C Compressor Push Button Switch Air conditioner is switched on and off with this push button switch. When air conditioning is switched on, the heater blower motor will always run in at least 1st speed When air conditioning is switched on, the additional fan will always run in at least Ist speed. Fresh Air/Circulated Air Push Button Switch When air conditioner is operated, it is used to switch fresh air or circulated air as desired. In the circulated air switch position the heater blower motor will always run in at least Ist speed.

64-50 DESCRIPTION OF AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM Switching on the air conditioner activates electromagnetic coupling (1) of compressor (2). Tho compressor (2) is now driven by the running engine. Compressor (2) increases the pressure of gaseous refrigerant (Frigon), which automatically causes the refrigerant temperature to also rise. The refrigerant puts off heat in condenser (3), through which it is condénsed (turns into a liquid). Drier (4) removes residual water from the refrigerant and absorbs it. Safety switches (5 and 6) stop the compressor when pressure is too high or too low". In this man- ner damage is prevented in the air conditioning system. Expansion valve (7) meters the amount of refrigerant which is injected into evaporator (8). The amount of refrigerant will depend on the temperature and pressure of refrigerant at outlet of the evaporator. The liquid refrigerant expands in evaporator (8) and is turned into gas. This change in state pro- duces strong cooling off of the refrigerant and evaporator. The fresh alr (or bypass circulation air) is cooled as it passes the evaporator, Freezing prevention switch (9) switches the compressor to prevent the formation of ice on the evaporator. Ice formation would reduce the cross section opening size and impair cooling efficiency. Moisture in the fresh air (or bypass circulation air) condenses on the evaporator and is discharged outside of car via lines on the transmission tunnel. This water is normal and not a sign of leakage. * See Specifications Main Components of Air Conditioner 1 = Pulley with electromagnetic coupling 2 = Compressor 3 = Condenser 4 = Drier 5 = Safety switch (low pressure pressostat) 6 = Safety switcti (high pressure pressostat) 7 = Expansion valve 8 = Evaporator 9 = Freezing prevention switch 10 = High pressure — gas 11 = High pressure — liquid 12 = Low pressure — liquid 13 = Low pressure — gas

s: 72 11 102 Removing and installing or replacing rear seat belt
t: 0 r2 09" 72-115 Checking Automatic Seat Belts: The automatic reel has two independent activat- ing systems for the locking effect. The first activating system should lock the reel when driving fast in curves, driving in tight curves, when car rolls over, during sharp brak- ‘ing or by impact, This activation is accomplished with a ball (1). To check, seat must be set upright and both hands placed on steering wheel in supporting Position. Then apply brakes fully while driving at a road speed equal to twice walking speed {road must be dry). The seat belt should lock. The second activating system is for additional safety and is controlled by inertia mass (2). If reel locks when pulling out belt suddenly, this system is also okay. The belt should retract automatically as far as possible when released, It could happen that the last section of the belt will have to be guided to the door beam by hand. If this last section is not wound, there could be @ weak or broken return spring (3) and/or exces- sive friction in the belt guides. An unusuable seat belt or a seat belt worn ina serious accident should be destroyed immedi ately after removal to guarantee that it cannot be used again. The automatic reel does not require servicing and must not be opened. 72072099 3072021 The automatic seat belt has to be replaced when the mounting bar (6) is bent or the stirrup is dis- torted in area (7). The stirrup must still pivot after mounting bolt has been tightened; only applicable to front seat belts, To fasten a belt the tongue should insert easily and engage in the lock with a loud click. When pushing in the “PRESS” button the belt tongue will be ejected from the lock by spring force. Replace seat belt when lock trim is missing or damaged. When replacing a seat belt also replace the lower strap, In the case of belts integrated in seats an impact could defform the lower strap stop on the seat rail. Never attempt to straighten the seat or seat rails. Deformed stirrups (1) must be replaced. If the plastic cover in the opening for the belt above the anchorage bar (16) has traces of wear, the seat belt must be replaced.
